Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, so you can just use the claim number.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was driving through the intersection in Sugar Land, Texas, heading east on the main road. The light had been
green for me when I entered.
Q: What happened next?
A: A vehicle coming from the cross street on my right pulled out and hit the driver's side of my car. It was a side
impact, and my car spun a little before stopping.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before it hit you?
A: Not really. I saw something move at the edge of my vision, but I didn't have time to react. I braked as hard as I
could.
Q: Were you injured?
A: Yes. My left wrist hit the door frame and the window area. I was taken by ambulance to the hospital, where they
found a fracture in my wrist. I've been wearing a splint and I can't grip things well right now.
Q: Did you have any passengers?
A: No, I was alone in the car.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I was following the traffic rules and I'm willing to provide my medical records and the repair estimate for
the car.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
A: Thanks.
</page>

"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
